title: Read any enum column of the warehouse import

blocks.text: The warehouse imports its inbound shipments from spreadsheets that people fill in by hand. Each enum column (the dock, the handling flags, the stage) is read with one shared helper, whatever enum the column holds, and the cells look like `north-gate`, ` Cold Store ` or `HAZMAT,OVERSIZE,FRAGILE`. The dashboard's "advance" button moves a shipment's stage to the next one with the same helper class.
`parseAll(...)` already splits a cell. Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Enums.java`:

items: `parse(...)`: the constant a cell's text means;
`next(...)`: the constant after the current one.

blocks.text: When you're done, every column parses the way people type its values, a cell's flags come back in the order the enum declares them, and "advance" works on every stage. About eight lines in total.
The tests use enums of their own, so the helper can't name any particular enum.

cases.says: a cell holding a constant's exact name parses, for each of several enums
text that names no constant is refused with IllegalArgumentException
a cell with several flags yields each named flag once
next gives the constant declared after the current one, and the first after the last
a name typed in another case, with spaces around it, or with a hyphen or space for the underscore, parses
a cell's flags come back in the order the enum declares them, not the order the cell lists them
next works from a constant that has a body of its own

origin.section: A Generic `parse` Reads Any Enum Through `getEnumConstants()`

concepts: getClass() of a constant with a body is an anonymous subclass whose getEnumConstants() is null; getDeclaringClass() is the enum for every constant.
A generic parse over Class<E>.getEnumConstants() reads any enum leniently and returns the caller's type; EnumSet.noneOf(type) keeps declaration order.
E extends Enum<E> admits any enum type and nothing else, and lets Enum's methods such as getDeclaringClass() return the caller's own type.
